    Past-only temporal features with explicit history

    Source: R/temporal-features.R
    epi_temporal_features.Rd

    Creates row-lag and past-window-mean features for numeric columns in .data. Optional history supplies earlier observations for the same groups and is used only as context; history rows are not returned. For each row, the lag is the value lag rows earlier, and the rolling mean uses the window rows immediately before the row, excluding the current value. Incomplete history or any missing value in the rolling window yields NA. Features are based on rows, not elapsed duration; no regular time spacing is inferred or filled.

    Usage

    epi_temporal_features(
  .data,
  ...,
  time,
  group = NULL,
  history = NULL,
  lag = 1L,
  window = 7L
)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped data frame of new observations in time order within each group.

    ...

    Tidy selection of one or more numeric feature columns.

    time

    A single numeric or Date time column, strictly increasing within each group in both .data and history.

    group

    Optional complete character, factor, logical, or numeric group column. With no group all rows form a single series.

    history

    Optional earlier data frame containing the selected features, time, and group columns with compatible types.

    lag

    Positive integer number of preceding rows to lag.

    window

    Positive integer number of preceding rows in the rolling mean.

    Value

    Input tibble in original order with lag{lag}_<column> and past_mean{window}_<column> columns. Existing output names are rejected.

    Details

    Within each group, time must be strictly increasing in both input datasets, and all matched history times must precede all .data times. Groups may be interleaved; output preserves .data order. History for groups absent from .data is ignored. time is numeric or a whole-day Date, with the same kind in both datasets. Missing feature values are permitted and propagated.

    This helper is outside recipes: it does not change the existing recipe steps' history behavior. For sequential one-step-ahead scoring it may use earlier observed values within .data. For a multi-step forecast made all at once, those later outcomes are not yet known; supplying them would leak future information. Supply only values actually available at each prediction time.

    Examples

    history <- data.frame(day = 1:3, cases = c(1, 2, 3))
new <- data.frame(day = 4:5, cases = c(4, 5))
epi_temporal_features(new, cases, time = day, history = history, lag = 1, window = 2)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>     day cases lag1_cases past_mean2_cases
#>   <int> <dbl>      <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1     4     4          3              2.5
#> 2     5     5          4              3.5
